newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA tax payments to rise 35 pct in 1997 - PDVSA.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA tax payments to rise 35 pct in 1997 - PDVSA.

text.p: Tax paid by Venezuela's state- owned oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) will rise by 35 percent in 1997 to $11.5 billion, a senior PDVSA executive said on Wednesday.
Ramon Espinasa, chief economist at PDVSA, said the figure represented the company's latest estimate and amounted to 14 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).

PDVSA reported record results in 1996, generating $8.5 billion in taxes and royalties, equivalent to 4 trillion bolivars using an exchange rate of 474 bolivars to the dollar. It also paid a 393 billion bolivar ($827 million) dividend in that year.
The 1997 dividend was expected at 1.1 trillion bolivars, Espinasa said, and added to the taxes and royalties would make $11.5 billion.
Venezuela has been increasing its oil production by 8-10 percent per year to take advantage of growing world demand for oil.
PDVSA's fiscal contribution this year would be equivalent to 5.6 trillion bolivars, Espinasa said at a meeting for the Foreign Press Association (APEX).

Espinasa said PDVSA plans a 20 percent production rise from 1996 to the end of 1998. Even if the average price falls to $15 per barrel from 1996's $18.5 per barrel average, Espinasa expected fiscal revenues to remain stable as production is forecast to rise to 3.7 million barrels per day in 1998.
